Spin only magnetic moment, $\mu_s=\sqrt{n(n+2)} \mathrm{BM}\begin{gathered}

questions.q: Valence electrons in the element $A$ are $3$ and that in element $B$ are $6$. Most probable compound formed from $A$ and $B$ is
questions.solution:
Valence electrons in $A = 3$

Valence electron in $B = 6$

Thus, $A$ is electropositive and $B$ is electronegative, $A$ can lose three electrons and $B$ can gain two electrons to attain stable configuration.

Hence, $A$ exist as $A^{3 +}$ and $B$ as $B^{2 -}$

$∴$ Compound formed is ${A}_{2}{B}_{3}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following are isoelectronic species?

I. $\overset{+}{C}{H}_{3}$

II. ${NH}_{2}^{-}$

III. ${NH}_{4}^{+}$

IV. ${NH}_{3}$
questions.solution:
I. Number of electrons in $\overset{+}{C}{H}_{3} = 6 + 3 - 1 = 8$

II. Number of electrons in ${NH}_{2}^{-} = 7 + 2 + 1 = 10$

III. Number of electrons in ${NH}_{4}^{+} = 7 + 4 - 1 = 10$

IV. Number of electrons in ${NH}_{3} = 7 + 3 = 10$

Since, species with same number of electrons are called isoelectronic species, Hence, $IInd, IIIrd$ and $IVth$ are isoelectronic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct bond order in the following species is:
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{O}_{2}^{+}$ ion - Total number of electrons
$(16-1)=15$
E.C.: $\begin{array}{r} \sigma1 s^{2} $\sigma^{*}$1 s^{2} $\sigma$2 s^{2} $\sigma^{*}$2 s^{2} $\sigma$2 p_z^{2} \\
\pi2 p_x^{2}=\pi2 p_y^{2} \pi^{*}2 p_x^{1}=\pi^{*}2 p_{y} \\
\text{ Bond order }=\frac{\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{b}}-\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{a}}}{2}=\frac{10-5}{2}=\frac{5}{2}=2 \frac{1}{2}
\end{array}\mathrm{O}_{2}^{-}$ (Super oxide ion): Total number of
electrons $(16+1)=17$
E.C.: $\begin{array}{l}\text{ \sigma1s }^{2} \sigma^{*}1 s^{2} $\sigma$2 s^{2} $\sigma^{*}$2 s^{2} $\sigma$2 p_z^{2} \\
\pi2 p_x^{2}=\pi2 p_y^{2} \pi^{*}2 p_x^{2}=\pi^{*}2 p_y^{1} \\
\text{ Bond order }=\frac{\left(\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{b}}-\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{a}}\right)}{2}=\frac{10-7}{2}=\frac{3}{2}=1 \frac{1}{2}
\end{array}\mathrm{O}_{2}^{2+}$ ion: Total number of electrons $=(16-2)=14$
E.C. $\begin{array}{l} \sigma1 s^{2} $\sigma^{*}$1 s^{2} $\sigma$2 s^{2} $\sigma^{*}$2 s^{2} \pi2 p_x^{2}=\pi2 p_y^{2} $\sigma$2 p_z^{2} \\
\text{ Bond order }=\frac{\left(N_{b}-N_{a}\right)}{2}=\frac{10-4}{2}=\frac{6}{2}=3
\end{array} So bond order: \mathrm{O}_{2}^{-}< \mathrm{O}_{2}^{+}< \mathrm{O}_{2}^{2+}$
